newsitem.title: USA: Japan's Sakakibara urges caution in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Sakakibara urges caution in Latin America.

text.p: A Japanese Finance Ministry official Tuesday urged caution in dealing with Latin American economies, saying that the basic structure in that region seems unchanged from before the Mexican debt crisis.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the International Finance Bureau of the Japanese Finance Ministry, told a development conference at the Inter-American Development Bank that the situation has improved since the Mexican crisis and that the markets are again becoming "somewhat euphoric" about the future of Latin economies.
"However, caution needs to be taken since the basic structure of the region seems unchanged -- low savings ratio supplemented by inflows of foreign capital, including hot money," Sakakibara said.
Turning to his own country, Sakakibara said Japan is "still struggling" to gets its financial sector back on track from its asset crisis.
